issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method signature is inconsistent: the problem statement (and the provided template Main usage) expects a no-argument method messageOnRide() that returns a String like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements it in Pig and Seal with a String parameter. This parameter mismatch will confuse students and prevents them from following the specified API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface match the problem specification and template usage by declaring String messageOnRide() with no parameters, and update Pig and Seal to implement the no-arg version returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an 'equipment' parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement and template Main (usage) to reflect messageOnRide(String equipment).

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() (Rideable.messageOnRide(): String), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements messageOnRide with a parameter in Pig and Seal. This signature mismatch changes the same conceptual operation (requesting the ride message) to a different method shape, causing students to be unable to map the required interface method from the problem/template to the solution implementation and leading to compilation/runtime confusion when calling messageOnRide() without arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's Rideable and all implementations (Pig, Seal) to define messageOnRide() with no parameters (returning the ride message), matching the problem description and template usage; or (B) update the problem statement and template (and any example calls) to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and document the equipment parameter so students implement the same signature.
